title: Acoustic Tweezers for Magnetic Skyrmions
abstract: Current methods for driving magnetic skyrmions predominantly translate ensembles as a whole, lacking single-particle selectivity. Here, we propose an "acoustic tweezer" that deterministically traps and routes individual skyrmions using spatially extended acoustic beams. We reveal that spatially confined longitudinal waves carry nontrivial phonon spin, inducing a magnetoelastic field whose chirality is locked to the acoustic spin texture. This generates polarity-selective radiation forces, distinct from conservative gradient forces, that attract skyrmions to local phonon spin maxima. Intersecting orthogonal beams create reconfigurable attractive points for adiabatic, deterministic manipulation. Our global-field-local-interaction paradigm establishes a non-destructive, on-chip route for high-precision topological spintronics.
summary: This paper introduces an 'acoustic tweezer' technique to deterministically manipulate individual magnetic skyrmions by exploiting magnetoelastic coupling with acoustic waves. By showing that confined longitudinal acoustic beams carry phonon spin, they generate a polarity-selective radiation force. This allows for the precise, non-destructive routing of topological magnetic textures on an chip.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is developing a method for deterministic, single-particle trapping and routing of magnetic skyrmions, overcoming limitations in current ensemble-based manipulation techniques.
main_result: The authors propose an 'acoustic tweezer' mechanism that uses the phonon spin carried by acoustic beams to generate polarity-selective radiation forces, enabling high-precision, non-destructive control over individual skyrmions.
method: The analysis involves deriving the magnetoelastic force ($\mathbf{F}_{	ext{mec}}$) from first principles, decomposing it into gradient and radiation components, and modeling the resulting dynamics using a generalized Thiele equation.
model_or_system: The system consists of magnetic skyrmions interacting with spatially extended longitudinal acoustic beams. The interaction is mediated by magnetoelastic coupling, which generates an effective field whose chirality is locked to the acoustic phonon spin texture.
key_observables: Polarity-selective radiation force; time-averaged force ($\langle \mathbf{F}_{	ext{mec}} angle_T$); Rayleigh dissipation rate ($\langle\dot{\mathcal{U}}angle_T$).
important_parameters: Acoustic wavelength ($\lambda$) comparable to skyrmion size ($R_{sk}$); the topological charge ($Q$) of the skyrmion.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a one-way coupling scheme, assuming the skyrmion drift velocity is much lower than the speed of sound; it also uses approximations like linear response theory and boundary condition assumptions for force integration.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate that positive phonon spin creates an attractive trapping line (red) while negative spin creates a repulsive line (blue), demonstrating polarity-selective attraction toward regions of maximum energy dissipation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the need for single-particle control, deriving the magnetoelastic force based on phonon spin angular momentum, establishing the radiation force mechanism via susceptibility analysis, and finally simulating deterministic trapping using intersecting beams to create reconfigurable points.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from acoustics/optics (tweezers) with condensed matter magnetism (skyrmions), providing a clear physical analogy for controlling quantum-like excitations in solid-state systems using external fields. The rigorous derivation of the radiation force component is particularly valuable for understanding non-conservative driving forces.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic of phonon-spin-mediated skyrmion interaction. A longitudinally polarized Gaussian acoustic beam propagates along +ˆx (light blue arrow). Transverse amplitude decay induces local- ized phonon spin angular momentum along ˆz (gradient-colored iso- surfaces), forming an attractive line (red, positive phonon spin) on the upper side and a repulsive line (blue, negative phonon spin) on the lower side. A Bloch skyrmion (Q = −1) exhibits polarity-selective responses: it is attracted toward the attractive line and repelled from the repulsive line, dictated by the signed coupling between skyrmion polarity and phonon spin orientation.
